```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(c4e.verbose = FALSE)
```

c4e turns the location of each household and the date of its interview into
two kinds of variables an economist adds to a survey:

* **weather extremes** over the period before the interview: hot, cold, wet
  and dry days, their spells, heatwaves and drought indices;
* **spatial controls** for the place: terrain, zones, distances, population
  density and climate normals.

Each comes from one call. This page shows the six calls on the small data
that ship with the package; the articles take each one apart.

```{r setup}
library(c4e)
```

## The data

A survey needs a household identifier, coordinates and an interview date.
The package ships 20 synthetic households at 12 locations, interviewed in
2023, and rasters over the same area: daily maximum temperature and
precipitation for 2021 to 2023, and monthly precipitation for 1984 to 2023.

```{r data}
survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
survey$interview <- as.Date(survey$interview)
head(survey)

tmax <- system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e")
pre_daily <- system.file("extdata", "pre_daily.tif", package = "c4e")
pre_monthly <- system.file("extdata", "pre_monthly.tif", package = "c4e")
```

## Weather extremes before each interview

`weather_extremes()` runs the whole chain: it places the households, reads the
raster, extracts the days at each location, flags the extremes, finds their
spells and summarises them over the year before each interview. A preset
picks the indicators; `list_presets()` shows them all.

```{r presets}
list_presets()[c("preset", "variable", "spec")]
```

The temperature raster is in kelvin; the `heat` preset reads its thresholds
in Celsius, so the data are converted first, and the history says so.

```{r heat}
heat <- weather_extremes(survey, tmax, id = hhid, interview = interview,
                         preset = "heat")
print(heat, n = 5)
```

`day_abv_30_sum` is the number of days above 30 C in the year before the
interview, `spell_abv_30_max` the longest run of them. Every table can print
the steps that produced it, ready to copy and adapt:

```{r history}
c4e_history(heat)
```

## Drought before each interview

`climate_indices()` computes the standardised precipitation index (SPI) on
monthly precipitation, or the SPEI when evapotranspiration is given, and
counts the months below drought thresholds. Here, the three-month SPI over
the six months before each interview:

```{r drought}
drought <- climate_indices(survey, pre_monthly, id = hhid, interview = interview,
                           preset = "drought_spi3",
                           window = window_lag("6 months"))
print(drought, n = 5)
```

## Spatial controls

`static_controls()` summarises layers that do not change: here an elevation
raster, from which slope, the terrain ruggedness index and roughness are
derived, and a zone raster, which is never averaged. Each radius adds a set
of columns.

```{r static}
template <- terra::rast(tmax)[[1]]
elevation <- terra::rast(template, vals = seq(500, 1550, length.out = 36))
zones <- terra::rast(template, vals = rep(1:3, 12))

static <- static_controls(survey, list(elevation = elevation, aez = zones),
                          id = hhid, buffer = c(0, 20000))
print(static, n = 5)
```

`time_varying_controls()` takes, for each household, the layer of the year
that matches its survey, here the population of the year before, and the
climate normals of the years before the survey:

```{r time-varying}
pop <- terra::rast(template, nlyrs = 3, vals = rep(c(100, 200, 300), each = 36))
terra::time(pop) <- as.Date(c("2021-01-01", "2022-01-01", "2023-01-01"))

controls <- time_varying_controls(survey, list(pop = pop), id = hhid,
                                  interview = interview, match = "previous_year",
                                  climate = list(tmax = tmax), years = 30,
                                  stats = c("mean", "sd"))
print(controls, n = 5)
```

## Every cell of a raster

The same indicators can be computed for every cell, per year or month, for
maps and grid panels. `grid_indicators()` returns a raster with one layer per
indicator and year:

```{r grid}
hot_years <- grid_indicators(tmax, preset = "heat", spells = FALSE)
names(hot_years)
terra::plot(hot_years[["day_abv_30_sum_2023"]],
            main = "Days above 30 C in 2023")
```

`grid_controls()` does the same for controls, such as the population density
within a radius:

```{r grid-controls}
density <- grid_controls(pop = pop[[3]], radius_m = c(0, 50000))
names(density)
```

## Export to Stata

`write_stata()` writes a `.dta` file with a label on every variable, built
from what each column measures, and optionally a codebook:

```{r stata}
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "heat.dta")
write_stata(heat, path, codebook = TRUE)
c4e_labels(heat)[1:4]
```

## Where next

* *Household extremes, step by step* takes `weather_extremes()` apart.
* *Relative extremes* uses percentiles instead of fixed thresholds.
* *Administrative divisions* computes the indicators by district.
* *Drought indices* covers the SPI and SPEI in detail.
* *Climatic parameters and spatial controls* builds controls by hand.
* *Grid indicators and maps* works on every cell of a raster.

For a project with several steps and large files, the
[targets](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) package reruns only what
changed. A `_targets.R` for the chain above:

```{r targets, eval = FALSE}
library(targets)
tar_option_set(packages = "c4e")

list(
    tar_target(survey_file, "data/survey.csv", format = "file"),
    tar_target(survey, {
        s <- read.csv(survey_file)
        s$interview <- as.Date(s$interview)
        s
    }),
    tar_target(tmax_file, "data/tmax_daily.tif", format = "file"),
    tar_target(heat, weather_extremes(survey, tmax_file, id = hhid,
                                      interview = interview, preset = "heat")),
    tar_target(heat_dta, {
        write_stata(heat, "output/heat.dta", codebook = TRUE)
        "output/heat.dta"
    }, format = "file")
)
```
